title: Surjectivity of the Stern-Brocot Encoding — the ℚ⁺ Bijection
description: Completes the open follow-up to the Stern-Brocot entry (OQ-03): proves surjectivity (every positive rational is reached by some left/right path) via the subtractive Euclidean algorithm, sharpens injectivity from states to rational values, and assembles the full bijection between binary paths and ℚ⁺. A constructive, duplicate-free enumeration of the positive rationals in lowest terms, with 0 axioms and 0 sorries.

overview.historicalContext: The Stern-Brocot tree (Stern 1858, Brocot 1861) is a binary tree containing every positive rational exactly once, already in lowest terms. The parent entry (OQ-03) formalized it as a state machine and proved coprimality, positivity, the BST ordering, and injectivity of the path-to-node map, explicitly leaving surjectivity — that every positive rational actually appears — as the open follow-up. Surjectivity is the half that turns the tree into a genuine enumeration of ℚ⁺, and it is classically obtained from the Euclidean algorithm: to locate p/q, repeatedly compare with the current mediant and descend left (smaller) or right (larger). Graham, Knuth, and Patashnik's 'Concrete Mathematics' presents exactly this search.
overview.problemStatement:
**Surjectivity of the Stern-Brocot Encoding (OQ-03-OQ-02)**

Prove that the Stern-Brocot tree reaches every positive rational, and combine with the parent's injectivity to obtain a bijection between binary left/right paths and ℚ⁺:

1. Surjectivity onto coprime pairs: every coprime (p,q) with p,q ≥ 1 is some node's (numerator, denominator)
2. Surjectivity onto ℚ⁺: every positive rational equals toRat of some path
3. Value injectivity: distinct paths give distinct rationals (sharpening state injectivity)
4. The bijection: range(toRat) = {x : ℚ | 0 < x} and toRat is injective
overview.text: Completes the Stern-Brocot enumeration of the positive rationals by proving surjectivity via the subtractive Euclidean algorithm and assembling the full bijection paths ≃ ℚ⁺. The reachability engine reach_aux expresses a target node in ancestor coordinates (a,b), so that the tree descent is exactly subtractive Euclid on (a,b) with a+b as the strictly decreasing measure.
overview.proofStrategy:
**Formalization Approach** (332 lines, 9 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms)

1. **The coordinate trick.** A det=1 state s = ⟨la,lb,ra,rb⟩ has left ancestor la/lb, right ancestor ra/rb, and mediant (la+ra)/(lb+rb). Any target node can be written uniquely as (num,den) = a·(la,lb) + b·(ra,rb) with a,b ≥ 1; the node itself is a = b = 1.

2. **reach_aux (surjectivity engine).** Strong induction on a+b. When a = b, coprimality forces a = b = 1 and the empty path works. When a > b, step left and recurse on (a−b,b); when a < b, step right and recurse on (a,b−a). This is exactly the subtractive Euclidean algorithm, and gcd(a,b) is preserved (so a = b never recurs except at 1).

3. **reach_root / toRat_surjective.** From the root init = ⟨0,1,1,0⟩ the target p/q has coordinates (q,p), so a+b = p+q. Specializing reach_aux gives every coprime pair; bridging an arbitrary positive rational to its reduced (num,den) gives every positive rational.

4. **Value injectivity.** The parent proved injectivity of the full 4-tuple state. Here two ℕ BST bounds (left_lt_mediant, mediant_lt_right), distilled from the parent's value_between_ancestors, show a left-subtree node is strictly below the parent mediant and a right-subtree node strictly above it. Equal values cannot straddle the mediant, giving mediant injectivity; coprimality of every node lifts this to toRat injectivity.

5. **The bijection.** toRat is injective and its range is exactly {x : ℚ | 0 < x}.
keyInsights: **Ancestor coordinates linearize the descent.** Tracking the target as (a,b) with (num,den) = a·(la,lb) + b·(ra,rb) turns the geometric tree search into pure subtractive Euclid: left is (a,b) ↦ (a−b,b), right is (a,b) ↦ (a,b−a). The measure a+b strictly decreases, and from the root it equals p+q — the familiar Euclidean quantity.

**Coprimality is exactly the termination certificate.** The subtractive step preserves gcd(a,b), which starts at 1 for a reduced target. So the only way to reach a = b is a = b = 1 — the node itself. Without coprimality the descent could stall at a = b = k > 1, which is precisely a non-reduced fraction k·(mediant).

**Surjectivity needs no determinant hypothesis.** reach_aux holds from ANY state, with no det = 1 assumption — the coordinate identities are purely formal. The determinant only re-enters when one wants the reached node to be in lowest terms (inherited from the parent).

**State injectivity vs value injectivity.** The parent proved different paths give different 4-tuple states; for a bijection of rationals one needs different paths give different VALUES. The gap is bridged by the BST ordering (a left node is below the mediant, a right node above) plus per-node coprimality recovering (num,den) from the rational.

**A choice-free, pairing-free ℚ⁺ enumeration.** Cantor's pairing enumerates ℚ but produces unreduced fractions and needs a skipping/reduction step. The Stern-Brocot bijection hits each positive rational exactly once, already in lowest terms, with the proof using only propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound — the ordinary foundational axioms.

Surjectivity IS the Euclidean algorithm: the tree descent to p/q is subtractive Euclid on the ancestor coordinates (a,b), and gcd-invariance of the subtractive step is exactly what makes the descent terminate at the reduced target.

sections.title: Module Header and Overview
sections.summary: Imports (including the parent module Proofs.DenumerabilityRationalsOQ03) and the module docstring: states the five deliverables (reach_aux, reach_root, toRat_surjective, value injectivity, the bijection), explains the coordinate trick, and records that Mathlib has no Stern-Brocot machinery.
sections.mathContext: Target node = a·(la,lb) + b·(ra,rb); left step (a,b) ↦ (a−b,b), right step (a,b) ↦ (a,b−a); from the root p/q has coordinates (q,p), so a+b = p+q.

sections.title: PART I: The Reachability Lemma (Surjectivity Engine)
sections.summary: reach_aux: from any state s and positive coprime coordinates (a,b), some path reaches the node a·(la,lb)+b·(ra,rb). Strong induction on a+b: a=b forces 1 (coprimality, empty path); a>b steps left; a<b steps right. reach_root specializes to the root, giving surjectivity onto coprime pairs.
sections.mathContext: Subtractive Euclid: gcd(a,b) preserved, a+b strictly decreases, base case a=b=1 = the mediant. Root coordinates of p/q are (q,p).

sections.title: PART II: Surjectivity onto the Positive Rationals
sections.summary: toRat_surjective: every positive rational equals toRat of some path. Bridges an arbitrary 0 < x to its reduced pair (x.num.natAbs, x.den) using Rat.num_pos, Rat.reduced, and Rat.num_div_den, then applies reach_root.
sections.mathContext: x > 0 ⟹ x = x.num/x.den with x.num.natAbs, x.den coprime and positive; reach_root produces the path.

sections.title: PART III: Injectivity of the Rational Value
sections.summary: left_lt_mediant and mediant_lt_right give ℕ cross-multiplied BST bounds (left subtree below mediant, right subtree above), distilled from the parent's value_between_ancestors. mediant_inj_gen proves value injectivity from any det=1 state by induction; same-direction recurses, opposite directions and nil-vs-cons contradict via the BST bounds. mediant_inj and toRat_injective lift to the root and to toRat, using per-node coprimality.
sections.mathContext: A left-subtree node n/d satisfies n·(lb+rb) < (la+ra)·d < right side; equal values cannot straddle the mediant. Equal reduced fractions ⟹ equal (num,den).

sections.title: PART IV: The Stern-Brocot Bijection
sections.summary: sternBrocot_bijection: toRat is injective and Set.range toRat = {x : ℚ | 0 < x}. Combines toRat_injective with toRat_surjective (and the parent's toRat_pos for the range inclusion).
sections.mathContext: toRat : Path → ℚ is a bijection onto ℚ⁺ — a constructive, duplicate-free, lowest-terms enumeration.

sections.title: PART V: Concrete Witnesses
sections.summary: Three existence witnesses from reach_root: paths encoding 2/3, 3/2, and the larger coprime pair 22/7 all exist, with coprimality discharged by decide.
sections.mathContext: 2/3 → [L,R], 3/2 → [R,L]; 22/7 is reached by a longer path matching its continued fraction [3;7].

conclusion.summary: Surjectivity of the Stern-Brocot tree is formalized (every positive rational is reached) via the subtractive Euclidean algorithm, value-map injectivity is established (sharpening the parent's state injectivity), and the two are combined into a bijection between binary left/right paths and the positive rationals — all with 0 sorries and 0 axioms. This completes the open follow-up posed by the parent entry and delivers a constructive, choice-free, lowest-terms enumeration of ℚ⁺.
conclusion.implications:
**1. A constructive ℚ⁺ enumeration.** range(toRat) = {x : ℚ | 0 < x} with toRat injective means the positive rationals are in explicit bijection with finite binary words, each rational appearing once and already reduced — no Cantor pairing, no reduction step, no choice beyond the foundational axioms.

**2. The Euclidean algorithm as a tree search.** reach_aux makes precise that locating p/q is subtractive Euclid on the ancestor coordinates; the path length is the sum of the continued-fraction coefficients of p/q.

**3. Toward the full bijection with ℕ.** Composing the path bijection with a breadth-first (or binary) enumeration of finite L/R words would give an explicit ℕ ≃ ℚ⁺, and hence ℕ ≃ ℚ, with strong structural guarantees.
openQuestions: Promote the surjective + injective pair to a bundled Equiv between {x : ℚ // 0 < x} and Path (or to ℕ via a BFS enumeration of paths).
Formalize the continued-fraction correspondence: the run-length encoding of the reach_aux path equals the continued-fraction coefficients of the target.
Extend from ℚ⁺ to all of ℚ by adjoining 0 and the negatives, yielding a constructive ℕ ≃ ℚ to compare with the Cantor-pairing entry.
